Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Instant lead response, qualification and routing

Leads from OEM portals, the website, ad lead forms, marketplaces, missed calls and WhatsApp are deduplicated, acknowledged within minutes where the buyer has opted in, qualified with a short flow and assigned to a consultant with a first-call timer.

New vehicle dealerships · Pre-owned vehicle dealers · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Dealerships pay for leads from several sources, but each source has its own portal and inbox. Leads that arrive after hours or during busy showroom periods wait, duplicates are called twice by different consultants, and buyers who hear nothing soon enquire at the next dealership.

Trigger

A new lead arrives from an OEM lead portal export or API, a website form, Meta or Google lead forms, a marketplace dealer panel, an IVR missed call or a click-to-WhatsApp chat.

How it runs

  1. Normalize the lead, match the mobile number against open DMS or CRM enquiries and merge duplicates, keeping every source for attribution.
  2. Check the consent captured on the source form; opted-in buyers receive an approved WhatsApp template, and everyone else becomes a call task.
  3. Run a short WhatsApp flow for model, variant or fuel, purchase timeframe, exchange and finance interest, and classify free-text questions without answering price or offer questions.
  4. Assign the lead by brand, branch, model and language, create or update the enquiry in the DMS or CRM and start a first-call timer.
  5. Alert the team leader in Slack when the timer lapses, and reassign after a second lapse under the rules the sales manager sets.
  6. Log source, response times and outcome for the weekly lead review.

Human checkpoint

The sales consultant makes the first call and answers anything about price, discounts, exchange value or finance. Team leaders handle reassignment, and the sales manager approves templates, qualifying questions and routing rules before launch and after every change.

Discover and enquireStandard4–6 weeks

Inspection-led listings synced to the website and marketplaces

Once a vehicle passes inspection and refurbishment, listing text is drafted from the structured inspection report, approved by the used-car manager and published to the website and marketplace dealer panels from one record. Reserved and sold vehicles come down everywhere.

Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Listings are typed separately into each portal, so descriptions vary, price changes reach some portals and not others, and sold cars keep attracting calls. Condition details depend on who wrote the listing, which leads to disputes after the sale.

Trigger

A vehicle's status changes to ready for sale, reserved, sold or repriced in the used-vehicle inventory record.

How it runs

  1. Pull the vehicle record: make, model, variant, year, odometer reading as recorded, ownership count, inspection findings and photos.
  2. Draft listing text from those fields only, with no claim that the inspection report does not support, and flag any missing disclosure.
  3. Route the draft, price and disclosures to the used-car manager for approval in the console.
  4. Publish to the dealer website and to each marketplace through the dealer feed, API or bulk upload template it offers, or prepare the listing for manual posting where it offers none, and record each listing ID.
  5. On reservation, sale or repricing, update or remove the listing on every channel, and send each marketplace's leads into the lead queue.

Human checkpoint

The used-car manager approves price, condition notes and disclosures such as accident, flood or repaint history before anything is published. Pricing suggestions are never applied automatically.

Test drive and evaluationStandard3–4 weeks

Test-drive and test-ride booking against the demo fleet

Buyers pick showroom or home test drives from slots tied to real demo-vehicle availability by variant and branch, get reminders and can reschedule in one tap. Consultants see the day's schedule and get a follow-up prompt after each drive.

New vehicle dealerships · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Demo vehicles are shared across consultants and branches and booked on a whiteboard or in a group chat. Double bookings, a demo vehicle away for service or a missed reminder lead to canceled drives, and buyers who did drive often get no structured next step.

Trigger

A buyer chooses a test drive in the qualifying flow or on the website, or a consultant requests a slot from the CRM.

How it runs

  1. Read demo-fleet availability by variant, fuel type and branch, excluding vehicles marked for service, charging or cleaning.
  2. Offer showroom slots, and home slots within the radius the showroom manager sets, then hold the vehicle and consultant on confirmation.
  3. Send an approved confirmation with location, documents to bring and a reschedule button, then a reminder before the slot.
  4. Prompt the consultant to check the original driving license in person and record start and end odometer readings.
  5. After the drive, ask one feedback question and create the consultant's next action, such as a quote or a second drive.

Human checkpoint

The consultant confirms every home test drive, checks the driving license before handing over keys and decides whether the drive goes ahead. The showroom manager sets the home-drive radius, time limits and which variants may leave the showroom.

Test drive and evaluationStandard3–5 weeks

Seller and exchange evaluation booking

Owners who want to sell or exchange share vehicle details and photos in a short WhatsApp flow, book a yard or doorstep inspection and receive an offer only after an evaluator has inspected the vehicle and a manager has approved the price.

Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Sell-my-car enquiries and exchange requests arrive by call and chat with incomplete details. Evaluators travel without the RC, service history or photos they need, and offers given over the phone before an inspection are later revised, which frustrates sellers.

Trigger

A seller enquiry arrives from the website, a marketplace or WhatsApp, or a new-vehicle consultant flags an exchange request in the CRM.

How it runs

  1. Collect registration number, model, year, kilometers driven, ownership count, loan status and photos through a WhatsApp flow.
  2. Offer yard or doorstep slots by evaluator and area, and send reminders listing the documents to keep ready.
  3. Give the evaluator a structured inspection checklist in an app, with photos and findings saved against the vehicle.
  4. Show the manager the inspection report, the evaluator's recommendation and comparable recent purchases from your own records.
  5. Send the approved offer with its validity period, and pass accepted vehicles to purchase and transfer paperwork.

Human checkpoint

The evaluator inspects every vehicle in person, and the used-car manager approves each offer price. No automated price is ever quoted to a seller.

Quote, finance and bookingAdvanced5–7 weeks

On-road quote with finance and insurance desk handoff

Consultants issue consistent on-road quotes from approved price lists and insurer quotes, with optional items shown as clear opt-ins. Finance and insurance requests move to the F&I desk with the buyer's consent, and lender disclosures and decisions stay with the lender.

New vehicle dealerships · Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Quotes are typed from price sheets, so one buyer can get different figures from different consultants, optional accessories look mandatory and discount approvals happen on calls. Finance interest is passed to lender executives on chat without consent or tracking, and nobody can see why a booking is waiting on the loan.

Trigger

A consultant marks a quote as requested in the CRM or DMS after a test drive or a pricing enquiry.

How it runs

  1. Assemble the quote from the approved price list, the state registration and road tax table, an insurer quote and selected accessories, with an issue date and validity period.
  2. Show accessories, extended warranty and add-on covers as separate optional lines the buyer chooses, never preselected.
  3. Route discounts or exchange bonuses above the consultant's limit to the sales manager for approval before the quote is sent.
  4. Send the quote as a secure link and record its version against the enquiry.
  5. On request and with consent, share the minimum details with the buyer's chosen lender through its DSA or sourcing channel, and track status to sanction and disbursal.
  6. Hand insurance to the dealership's designated insurance executive, log the insurer, cover and add-ons the buyer chooses, and record when the buyer arranges cover elsewhere.

Human checkpoint

The sales manager approves discounts and exchange values above limits. The lender makes every credit decision and issues its Key Facts Statement; the dealership shows EMIs only as indicative. The designated insurance executive explains cover and add-ons, and the buyer chooses the insurer and cover.

Allotment, paperwork and deliveryStandard4–6 weeks

Booking-to-delivery tracker with waiting-period updates

Every booking gets one tracker for allotment, payments, loan disbursal, insurance, registration, accessories and pre-delivery inspection. Buyers get regular status updates in approved wording, and coordinators see what is blocking each delivery.

New vehicle dealerships

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

On popular models buyers wait weeks or months, and status lives in the OEM allocation portal, the DMS, the finance desk and the accessories team. Buyers call for updates, consultants guess dates, and silence or a missed promise often ends in a canceled booking.

Trigger

A booking amount is receipted in the DMS against a model, variant and color.

How it runs

  1. Create the delivery record with milestones for allotment, payment, loan disbursal, insurance, registration, accessories, PDI and handover, each with a named owner.
  2. Read allocation and in-transit status from OEM portal exports, and update milestones as owners mark them done.
  3. Send the buyer a scheduled waiting-period update in approved wording; a delivery date is shared only after the delivery coordinator confirms allotment.
  4. Alert the milestone owner and the delivery coordinator when an item stalls beyond the agreed number of days.
  5. Offer delivery slots once every milestone is complete, and send a handover checklist with the documents to bring.

Human checkpoint

The delivery coordinator confirms allotment and every delivery date before it reaches the buyer. Any change to a promised date, or a request to switch model or color, goes to the sales manager.

Allotment, paperwork and deliveryStarter2–4 weeks

Registration, HSRP and RC status tracking

After invoicing, each vehicle's registration checklist, Vahan application, tax payment, number plate fitment and RC dispatch are tracked with a named owner. Buyers get status updates, and registration staff see what is missing before the file is submitted.

New vehicle dealerships · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Registration depends on correct buyer documents, insurance, tax payment and each state's process, followed by HSRP fitment and RC dispatch. Missing documents surface late, temporary registrations run close to expiry, and buyers call the showroom to ask where their plates and RC are.

Trigger

The vehicle invoice is generated in the DMS, or a temporary registration is issued.

How it runs

  1. Create the registration checklist for the buyer's state and vehicle category, including identity and address proof, PAN or Form 60, insurance and hypothecation details.
  2. Collect missing documents through a secure upload link that asks for masked Aadhaar where it is accepted, and queue them for staff verification.
  3. Record the Vahan application number and status that the registration executive enters after submission.
  4. Track tax and fee payment, registration number allotment, HSRP fitment appointment and RC dispatch, updating the buyer at each step.
  5. Alert the registration lead when a file stalls or a temporary registration nears its end date.

Human checkpoint

The registration executive verifies every document and submits each application on Vahan personally; the automation never submits to a government portal. Name mismatches, other-state addresses and company registrations go to the registration lead.

Allotment, paperwork and deliveryStandard4–5 weeks

Ownership transfer and RC document tracker for used vehicles

Every vehicle bought or sold gets a transfer file covering Form 29C intimation, Forms 29 and 30, hypothecation removal and NOCs, with reminders to whoever owes the next document and alerts before statutory reporting windows close.

Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

A used vehicle passes from seller to dealer to buyer, often with a loan to close, an NOC from another state and documents from three parties. When files stall, the RC still shows the previous owner, liability is unclear and buyers chase the dealer for months.

Trigger

A purchase from a seller or a sale to a buyer is closed in the used-vehicle DMS or inventory record.

How it runs

  1. Open a transfer file recording the vehicle, the parties, any loan, the state of registration and the acknowledgment number of the Form 29C intimation signed by owner and dealer on Vahan.
  2. Generate the document checklist for the case, such as Forms 29 and 30, Form 35 and the lender NOC for financed vehicles, a Form 28 NOC for other-state transfers, insurance and PUC.
  3. Check for pending challans, lapsed insurance or PUC and open hypothecation, collect documents through secure links, and record the documentation executive's verification of each item.
  4. Remind whoever owes the next document, and alert the manager as the seller's and buyer's reporting windows under Section 50 of the Motor Vehicles Act approach.
  5. Update the buyer when the Vahan application is filed and when the new RC is issued, and prompt the insurance transfer to the new owner.

Human checkpoint

The documentation executive checks identities and signatures and files every application on Vahan; the automation only tracks and reminds. The used-car manager handles exceptions such as pending challans, lender delays or disputes.

Allotment, paperwork and deliveryStandard3–5 weeks

EV subsidy document checks and ownership onboarding

For eligible EV sales, the model is checked against the current PM E-DRIVE list, buyer details are checked before the e-voucher is generated, and signed e-voucher status is tracked. New owners then get approved onboarding messages on charging, range, app pairing and first service.

EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Scheme eligibility, incentive rates and end dates change by notification, and the e-2W incentive briefly lapsed in August 2026 before it was extended. A name or mobile mismatch between the invoice and the Aadhaar-authenticated e-voucher can hold up the claim, and new EV owners call with the same charging and range questions in their first weeks.

Trigger

An EV booking is converted to an invoice in the DMS.

How it runs

  1. Check that the incentive is open and funded, and check the model and variant against the current PM E-DRIVE eligible list and any state EV benefit, using the list the subsidy administrator maintains.
  2. Compare the buyer's name and mobile number on the invoice with the details to be used for e-KYC, and flag mismatches before the e-voucher is generated.
  3. Track e-voucher generation, buyer signature, dealer signature and upload for each vehicle, and alert the administrator to gaps before delivery.
  4. After handover, send a short series on charging practice, home charger installation booking, app pairing, range and the first service.
  5. Route owner questions to a trained staff member, and log recurring questions to improve the content.

Human checkpoint

The buyer completes Aadhaar authentication and signs the e-voucher on the scheme's own process, and the dealership's subsidy administrator signs, uploads and resolves any mismatch. The service manager approves charging and battery content in line with the OEM's guidance.

Service and repairStarter2–4 weeks

Service, PUC and battery check reminders by date and distance

Due dates are calculated per vehicle from the OEM schedule, the last service and average daily kilometers from job-card odometer readings. Consenting owners get reminders with one-tap booking, and owners who stop coming go to a call list.

Service centres & workshops · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Fixed-date reminders ignore how much a vehicle is driven, reminders stop after the free services, and nobody follows up owners who quietly move to local garages. EV owners also need battery and software checks that differ from engine service schedules.

Trigger

A daily job finds vehicles whose estimated service due date, PUC expiry or EV battery check falls inside the reminder window.

How it runs

  1. Calculate the next due date from the OEM schedule, the last service date and average kilometers per day from the job-card history.
  2. Check purpose-wise consent and channel preference, and skip owners with an open job or a recent visit.
  3. Send the reminder as an approved template, in the category Meta assigns, with booking buttons and one follow-up if there is no reply.
  4. Book straight into the service schedule when the owner picks a slot, or create a call task for the customer relationship executive.
  5. Move owners who miss two service cycles to a lapsed-owner call list with their service history.

Human checkpoint

Customer relationship executives call lapsed owners and handle every reply that is not a simple booking. The service manager sets reminder windows and frequency limits, and approves EV check content in line with the OEM's guidance.

Service and repairStandard4–5 weeks

Online service booking with pick-up and drop

Owners book on WhatsApp or the website against advisor and bay capacity, describe concerns in their own words and request pick-up. Drivers get assigned runs and record timestamped condition photos, and owners can follow the vehicle until it is back.

Service centres & workshops

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Bookings arrive by phone and land in an advisor's diary, so bays are overbooked on some days and idle on others. Pick-up and drop is coordinated by calls, drivers arrive outside the promised window, and missing condition photos turn small scratches into disputes.

Trigger

An owner books from a reminder, the website or WhatsApp, or an advisor creates a booking with pick-up requested.

How it runs

  1. Offer slots based on advisor capacity, bay types and parts availability for common jobs, and capture the owner's concerns as free text.
  2. Summarize the concerns into a draft job description for the advisor to confirm with the owner.
  3. For pick-ups, check the address is within the service radius, assign a driver and time window, and send the owner the driver's name and a tracking link.
  4. At pick-up, have the driver record timestamped photos, odometer and fuel or charge level, with the owner's acknowledgment.
  5. When the vehicle is ready, send the invoice link and payment options, schedule the drop and repeat the condition record at handover.

Human checkpoint

The service advisor confirms every booking and job description with the owner before work begins. Drivers walk around the vehicle with the owner, and any damage disagreement goes to the works manager.

Service and repairStandard4–6 weeks

Job-card status and customer approval for additional work

When technicians find additional work, the advisor sends an itemized estimate with photos or video, and the owner approves or declines each line. Work starts only after approval is recorded, and the owner gets status updates until the vehicle is ready.

Service centres & workshops · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Advisors spend hours calling owners for approval, vehicles wait in bays while calls go unanswered, and verbal approvals lead to billing disputes. Declined work is forgotten, so safety-related advice is never followed up.

Trigger

A technician records an additional finding on the job card in the DMS or workshop software.

How it runs

  1. Notify the advisor with the finding, the technician's photos or video and the parts and labor lines priced from the DMS.
  2. Draft a plain-language explanation of each item for the advisor to edit and approve.
  3. Send the owner a secure estimate link with approve and decline buttons per line, the revised delivery time and the advisor's contact.
  4. Record each decision with a timestamp and the verified mobile number, update the job card and hold any line without a recorded approval.
  5. Send updates when work is complete, during washing and when the vehicle is ready, and log declined items for the next reminder.

Human checkpoint

The service advisor reviews every estimate and explanation before it is sent, and the owner approves or declines each line. Safety-critical findings such as brakes or battery faults also get a call from the advisor, and estimates above an agreed amount need the works manager's sign-off.

Feedback, renewals and upgradeStandard3–4 weeks

Post-delivery and post-service feedback with service recovery

A short feedback request follows each delivery and service visit. Low ratings, repeat concerns and complaints become tickets with the job or sale history attached, and a named person calls the owner back within the agreed time.

Service centres & workshops · Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Dealerships collect ratings, often for OEM surveys, but unhappy owners rarely get a call. Repeat repairs and post-sale complaints about used vehicles surface first in public reviews or consumer complaints instead of on a manager's desk.

Trigger

A vehicle is handed over after a sale or a service visit, and the delivery or gate pass is closed in the DMS.

How it runs

  1. Wait the agreed interval, then send one or two questions and an optional comment box.
  2. Classify comments by theme, such as delay, billing, workmanship, staff or vehicle condition, and summarize them for the ticket.
  3. Open a ticket for low ratings, complaints or a repeat visit for the same concern within the agreed period, with the job card or sale details attached.
  4. Assign the call-back to the customer relations manager, and to the works manager or used-car manager for workmanship or condition issues.
  5. Track call-back, resolution and any goodwill decision, and report themes monthly by advisor, workshop and model.

Human checkpoint

The customer relations manager calls every flagged owner, and the works manager or used-car manager decides on rework, refunds or goodwill. Staff never ask owners to change or inflate OEM survey ratings.

Tools

WBWhatsApp Business PlatformTTypeformnn8nACAnthropic ClaudeMPMicrosoft Power BI

Systems it connects

  • DMS delivery and job-card records
  • OEM customer satisfaction survey program
  • Complaint register

Data & consent

Uses owner contact, visit details, ratings and comments. Comments are classified without sending the owner's identity to the model. Tickets keep the history needed for resolution and follow the dealership's retention period. One feedback request is sent per visit.

What we deliver

  • Feedback templates and timing rules
  • Recovery ticket queue with call-back alerts
  • Theme classification with weekly accuracy checks
  • Monthly recovery report

How we measure it

  • Service recovery closure time
  • Repeat repair rate
  • Flagged owners called back on time
  • Complaint themes by workshop

Feedback, renewals and upgradeStarter3–4 weeks

Consented insurance renewal and extended-warranty reminders

Owners who agreed to renewal messages get reminders before policy and warranty expiry. Insurance renewals go to the designated insurance executive for owners the dealership may serve under its insurer appointment, and extended warranties are offered only while the vehicle is eligible.

New vehicle dealerships · Service centres & workshops

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Renewal dates sit in insurer portals and DMS fields, so owners hear from aggregators first and lapses go unnoticed. Extended-warranty eligibility windows close before anyone mentions them, and blanket calls to owners who never agreed to them break consent and TRAI preference rules.

Trigger

A daily job finds policies or standard warranties expiring within the windows the dealership sets.

How it runs

  1. Read policy and warranty expiry dates from the DMS and the insurer or MISP records.
  2. Check consent for renewal messages, the owner's call preferences and whether the owner may be served under the dealership's insurer appointment.
  3. Send a reminder with the expiry date and a request-a-quote button; no premium is quoted automatically.
  4. Create a task for the designated insurance executive to prepare quotes in the insurer system and discuss cover with the owner.
  5. For extended warranty or accessories, check the OEM's eligibility window, kilometer limit and the owner's opt-in to offers, then send a marketing template or raise it at the next service visit.

Human checkpoint

The designated insurance executive explains cover, add-ons and premiums, and the owner chooses. Warranty eligibility and claims are decided under the OEM's terms by the warranty in-charge, not by the automation.

Uses owner contact, policy expiry, insurer name and warranty dates. Claims history is not used for targeting. Reminders stop on opt-out or on renewal elsewhere, and calls and SMS respect DND and the owner's TRAI preference settings.

  • Approved renewal and warranty templates
